verdict: Walmart's revenue rose 5.5% to $169.6B and operating income grew 8.2% as U.S. comparable sales rose 5.3% — and headline profit jumped to $4.6B from $0.5B a year ago, when a $4.75B paper loss on investment stakes crushed it.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: The big U.S. stores — comparable sales up 5.3% on more transactions and bigger baskets, with eCommerce contributing about 290 basis points of the comp.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores and e-commerce outside the U.S., including Flipkart in India — net sales up 8.0% in dollars and 12.4% in constant currency.

segments.name: Sam's Club U.S.
segments.note: The warehouse-club business — net sales up 7.2% excluding fuel, with comparable sales up 7.0% excluding fuel, led by food and health & wellness.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Sam's Club membership fees plus advertising (the global advertising business grew 28%) and other income.

opex.name: Operating, selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the stores, the supply chain and the back office.

otherDetail: Interest of $478M, net, plus a $132M loss on equity and other investments — mostly fair-value moves. A year ago that investments line was a $4,750M loss, which is why the year-ago profit was so small.
footerNote: Net profit shown is the $4,577M attributable to Walmart; consolidated net income was $4,714M, of which $137M belongs to noncontrolling interests.
follow100Note: Walmart keeps just $2.70 of every $100 — but on $169.6B of quarterly revenue that is still $4.6B. A year ago the same quarter kept only about $0.30 of every $100, after a $4.75B paper loss on investment stakes.

takeaways.title: Stores earned faster than sales
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 8.2% to $6.7B — faster than sales — as the gross margin rate improved 21 basis points, membership income grew, and eCommerce losses shrank.

takeaways.title: eCommerce and ads surged
takeaways.text: Global eCommerce sales grew 27%, led by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery and the marketplace, and the global advertising business grew 28% — newer, higher-margin income streams growing far faster than the stores.

takeaways.title: Full-year guidance lifted
takeaways.text: Walmart raised its FY25 outlook: net sales growth of 4.8% to 5.1% and adjusted operating income growth of 8.5% to 9.25% in constant currency.

oneTimers: Other (gains) and losses was a $132M loss on equity and other investments — mostly fair-value moves. Adjusted EPS of $0.58 excludes a $0.01 net-of-tax loss from these items. A year ago the same line was a $4,750M loss, which cut that quarter's attributable profit to $453M.
